Course Objective
Physics is the science from which all technologies have evolved. Engineers deal with various
technologies which eventually leads to new innovations and improvements. This course is
designed to impart a thorough knowledge of the basic principles along with the applied aspects
of the same, which help students to understand, apply and contribute to evolving technologies
more effectively and thereby improve the standard of life and the society.

Course Objective
Engineers communicate using engineering graphics. Graphical language is used to describe ideas and convey
directions for tasks on the shop floor and other locations. This course will help students improve their
drafting and drawing skills. It includes graphics theory, standards & conventions of drawing, the tools of
drawing and the use of drawings in engineering applications. The curriculum aims at developing the ability
to draw and read various engineering curves, projections and dimensioning styles.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students would be able to -
1. Draw engineering curves, projection of lines and planes
2. Apply principles of orthographic projections for drawing given pictorial views and draw isometric
views from orthographic projections using CAD software
3. Construct free hand sketches of given engineering elements
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Basic Elements of Drawing   02
Drawing instruments and supporting material: method to use them with applications,
standard sizes of drawing sheets, convention of lines and their applications,
dimensioning techniques - types and applications.
2.   Engineering Curves   07
Concept and understanding of focus, directrix, vertex and eccentricity. Conic sections -
methods to draw an ellipse by directrix-focus method, methods to draw a parabola by
directrix-focus method, methods to draw a hyperbola by directrix-focus method,
methods to draw involutes for circle and pentagon.
3.   Projection of Lines and Planes   07
Projection of straight lines inclined to one plane and parallel to the other plane, Projection
of plane surfaces inclined to one reference plane and parallel to the other plane.
4.   Orthographic Projections   06
Introduction of projections - orthographic and isometric, concept and applications, first
angle method of projection, conversion of pictorial view into orthographic views of
simple objects – object containing plain surfaces, slanting surfaces, slots, ribs, cylindrical
surfaces.

available, draw basic entities like Line, Circle, Arc, Polygon, Ellipse, Rectangle and
Polyline, Modify and edit commands like trim, delete, copy, offset, layers, Linear,

having plain, slanting, cylindrical surfaces and slots on slanting surfaces.

and Looping. Enable students solve complex problems using the knowledge of Arrays,
Functions, and Pointers.
Course Outcomes

Prerequisite: Engineering Mechanics
Course Objective
This course focuses on the conventional machines and kinematics involved in machines.   It
intends to help the students understand the turning moment diagrams of IC engines and the
gyroscopic couples of different automobiles.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, the student will be able to -
1. Describe the fundamentals of link, machines, and mechanism.
2. Analyze the degree of freedom in mechanisms and its implications
3. Create an application based simple four bar mechanism using CAD modelling
4. Determine velocity in a four-bar linkage mechanism
5. Illustrate and interpret turning moment diagrams for engines equipped with flywheels
6. Apply the principle of gyroscopic couples to ensure the stability of airplanes and ships
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Simple Mechanisms   13
Introduction, Kinematic Link or Element, Types of Links, Structure,
Difference Between a Machine and a Structure, Kinematic Pair, Types of
Constrained Motions, Classification of Kinematic Pairs, Kinematic Chain,
Types of Joints in a Chain, Mechanism, Number of Degrees of Freedom for
Plane Mechanisms.
Application of Kutzbach Criterion to Plane Mechanisms, Grubler’s Criterion
for Plane Mechanisms, Inversion of Mechanism, Types of Kinematic Chains,
Four Bar Chain or Quadric Cycle Chain, Grashof’s Law, Inversions of Four
Bar Chain
2.   Mechanisms with Lower Pairs   .   07
Introduction, Pantograph, Study working and applications of Straight Line
Mechanism such as-Peaucellier mechanism, Watts mechanism, Modified
Scott-Russel mechanism, Grasshopper mechanism. Study of steering gear
mechanism, Universal or Hooke's Joint, Double Hooke's Joint with its
application.

3.   Velocity in Mechanisms   08
Introduction to Instantaneous Centre Method (ICR), Space and Body
Centrodes, Velocity of a Point on a Link by Instantaneous Centre Method,
Properties of the Instantaneous Centre, Number of Instantaneous Centres in
a Mechanism, Types of Instantaneous Centres, Location of Instantaneous
Centres, Aronhold Kennedy (or Three Centres in Line) Theorem, Method of
Locating Instantaneous Centres in a Mechanism for 4 links
4.   Turning Moment Diagram and Flywheels   09
Working principle of internal combustion engines, turning moment diagram
for a single cylinder double acting steam engine, turning moment diagram
for a four-stroke cycle internal combustion engine, turning moment diagram
for a multi-cylinder engine, fluctuation of energy, determination of
maximum fluctuation of energy, coefficient of fluctuation of energy,
coefficient of fluctuation of speed, energy stored in the flywheel, dimension
of flywheel rim.
5.   Gyroscope and its applications   08
Introduction, Precessional Angular Motion, Gyroscopic Couple, Effect of
Gyroscopic Couple on an Aeroplane, Terms Used in a Naval Ship, Effect of
Gyroscopic Couple on a Naval Ship during Steering, Effect of Gyroscopic
Couple on a Naval Ship during Pitching, Effect of Gyroscopic Couple on a
Navel during Rolling.
Total   45

8 to 10 experiments based on the syllabus.

Course Objectives
To equip students with industry exposure, enabling them to understand various industrial
aspects, identify key challenges, analyze situations, and effectively solve engineering problems
relevant to the industry.
Course Outcomes
After completing the course, students will be able to:
1. Describe industrial practices and work culture to bridge the gap between theory and
practice with insights from industry professionals.
2. Demonstrate effective communication skills to comprehend and engage in industrial
practices.
3. Identify and follow discipline, safety norms, and environmental regulations in an industrial
setting.
4. Interpret and analyse industrial problems to suggest appropriate solutions.
5. Collaborate effectively within a team to achieve common industrial objectives.
6. Recognize the importance of lifelong learning and adaptability in a dynamic industrial
environment.
Guidelines
Internship Trainee’s Code of Conduct:
Trainee is required to:
a. Join on the stated date and complete the training as specified by the industry.
b. Fill the Joining Report, get it endorsed by the concerned Industry Official and email the
scanned copy within three days of joining to the Placement Department and Faculty
Mentor.
c. Adhere to all the rules and regulations, safety norms of the industry and thereby ensure
professional conduct.
d. Take instructions from the Industry Mentor on a daily basis and complete the same with
due diligence and quality.
e. Fill the Weekly logbook, get it endorsed by the concerned Industry Official and
f. then email the scanned copy to the Faculty Mentor on regular basis.

Mentoring process:
a. Every trainee shall be allocated two Mentors: An Industry Mentor and a Faculty from
the Department (appointed by Head of the Department).
b. Faculty Mentor shall connect with the Industry Mentor and the Trainee on a Periodic basis.
Training Report:
a. Students should take guidance from faculty and industry mentor and prepare a report on
their work done during internship and one copy should be submitted to the Institute.
b. The report should be prepared in a format prescribed by the University.
Interim Presentation
It should give an overview of the training to be done.
Report: Interim Report (IR)
(One copy to be submitted each to internal mentor & Company Mentor)
This report must cover the following aspects:
a.   Synopsis: A statement of about 100 words describing what the training is about.
b. Goals: Stating what the training will accomplish
c.   Schedule: A time frame indicating steps that will be required and the expected date when
they will be completed.
d. Reference: Bibliography and internet materials referred.
Final Presentation
The Final Presentation will evaluate the students in terms of the following
a. Knowledge of basic concepts
b.   Ability to identify and analyze the problem
c.   Ability to apply the knowledge to solve the problem
d.   Systematic progression of the subject matter
e.   Effective oral communication
Final Training Report
(One copy to be submitted each to Institute& Company Mentor)
The Report (Interim Report and Final Report), which is the written component of evaluation, is
judged for the following points.
a.   Comprehensive study of the problem & objective
b.   Methodology and implementation
c.   Ability to analyze the problem
d.   Logical sequencing, organizing and data handling
